scenario: Five independent platform owners each hold their own slice of lifecycle evidence for one change; the composition resolves end to end through opaque native cross-references with no central workflow record, and removing any one module leaves the others' results intact.

platforms.holds: the story and its acceptance decision
the pull request, review, and merge evidence
build, test, and artifact evidence for the change
platforms.reference_kind: build slug + artifact references, status posted to the source host

platforms.holds: runtime controls and deployment audit trail
deployment and operation telemetry, correlated by correlation ids

cross_references: work item cites the pull request URL
pull request cites the commit SHA; CI posts build status to it
deployment audit cites the build artifact reference
telemetry correlates by correlation ids that carry no authority

when: a fresh session inspects the change's lifecycle state starting from only the work-item reference

reasons: every capability's result resolves through its owning platform's native records
the inspection reconstructs the full chain by following opaque cross-references
each platform's evidence identifies source, actor, native revision, and freshness
must_not: introduce a central workflow database, universal envelope, or sidecar record
normalize one platform's identifiers into another's schema
break sibling results when any one platform module is uninstalled
use long-lived static credentials for the CI-to-cloud link
